response.title: Harborlight FY2026 Results and a Sixth Site Plan

segments.heading: The main point
segments.text: Harborlight served more adults in fiscal year 2026. Now staff want to grow again by opening a sixth site. They recommend that the board approve an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000. The budget adds a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library. It also adds two site coordinators. Staff estimate the new site would serve 180 more learners a year. The facts behind this request come next.

segments.heading: Who we served
segments.text: Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners in fiscal year 2026. The year before, it enrolled 936. Learners studied at five neighborhood sites. Of them, 412 worked toward a high school equivalency credential. Another 389 were English language learners. Sixty-eight percent of learners who stayed at least 12 weeks gained one or more reading levels on the CASAS assessment. Seventy-one learners earned a high school equivalency credential. No year in the organization's history saw more.

segments.heading: The people behind the work
segments.text: Volunteer tutors carry a big share of the work. A corps of 214 volunteer tutors gave 9,870 tutoring hours. The average tutor stayed 14 months. Harborlight also employs 11 full-time staff. Four of them are site coordinators. One learner at the Riverside site described what this work means in a few words. Quote. "I read my granddaughter a bedtime story for the first time this spring." End quote.

segments.heading: Where the money went
segments.text: FY2026 operating expenses came to $1,420,000. Program costs made up 81 percent of spending. Foundation grants brought in $640,000. Individual donors gave $388,000. The city's adult education contract paid $295,000. Each learner cost $1,237 to serve. There is one caution. The treasurer reported that reserves stand at 3.2 months of operating expenses. The board's target is 4 months, so reserves fall short.

segments.heading: Adults still waiting
segments.text: Many adults still wait for a seat. At year end, 287 adults were on the waitlist. Most were waiting at the Eastgate and Riverside sites. The average wait lasted nine weeks. Staff believe a sixth site would help with this. By their estimate, it would serve 180 more learners a year. They also estimate it would cut the waitlist in half.

segments.heading: The board's requests
segments.text: The board made two requests at the September 13 retreat. First, staff should bring a one-page summary of the FY2027 budget request to the October 21 board meeting. Second, board members asked for a short deck. They plan to use it when they talk with funders about the sixth site. The board also agreed to vote on the FY2027 budget on October 21.

response.recap: Remember three things. First, Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners in FY2026, up from 936. Seventy-one of them earned a high school equivalency credential. Second, 287 adults were on the waitlist at year end, and reserves stand at 3.2 months, below the target of 4 months. Third, staff recommend a $1,610,000 FY2027 budget that adds a sixth site at Eastgate.
